subject: Media Literacy
title: The Birth of Modern Advertising
description: A quick, practical guide to The Birth of Modern Advertising.

hook.text: In the 1920s, Listerine invented a disease — halitosis — then sold the cure. Sales jumped 7,000%.

buildup.text: Modern advertising doesn't just sell products. It identifies problems you didn't know you had.

discovery.text: The shift from informational ads to emotional manipulation began in the early 20th century with Edward Bernays.

twist.text: Bernays was Sigmund Freud's nephew. He used his uncle's psychology to manipulate consumer desire.

climax.text: Advertising became less about what a product does and more about how it makes you feel.

punchline.text: They don't sell products. They sell feelings about products.

quiz.question: What did Listerine do to boost sales in the 1920s?
options: Invented the term 'halitosis' to create a problem they could solve
